BSL 305.description: Examines business ethics, stakeholder responsibilities and legal compliance through ethical decision-making cases.

review.rationale: Examines business ethics, stakeholder responsibilities and legal compliance through ethical decision-making cases. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

BUS 200.name: Introduction to Business
BUS 200.description: Introduces business functions, competitive strategies and organizational decisions across economics, finance, marketing and management.
BUS 200.prerequisites: Requisite: Non Business Majors. The description limits this to general-education credit; the explicit requisite is nonbusiness majors.

review.rationale: Introduces business functions, competitive strategies and organizational decisions across economics, finance, marketing and management. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

BUS 201.name: Money
BUS 201.description: Develops personal-finance literacy in budgeting, credit, investments, insurance, housing and retirement planning.
BUS 201.prerequisites: The description states no credit toward any business major or minor.

review.rationale: Develops personal-finance literacy in budgeting, credit, investments, insurance, housing and retirement planning. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

BUS 202.description: Studies legal institutions, property rights, regulation and societal obligations affecting businesses.

review.rationale: Studies legal institutions, property rights, regulation and societal obligations affecting businesses. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

BUS 204.description: Combines corporate sustainability practice with governance, citizenship and institutional responsibilities.

review.rationale: Combines corporate sustainability practice with governance, citizenship and institutional responsibilities. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

BUS 206.prerequisites: The description identifies nonbusiness students as the audience, without an explicit enrollment-prohibition field.

review.rationale: Examines international business operations and the institutional conditions affecting multinational firms. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

CSC 506.name: Logic and Automated Reasoning
CSC 506.description: Combines formal logic and incompleteness with resolution, proof-search methods and automated theorem-proving systems.
CSC 506.prerequisites: Prerequisite: CSC317 or CSC545 and MTH309 or MTH230.

review.rationale: The description gives substantial attention both to mathematical logic and to automated-reasoning methods; neither component is reduced to an incidental application.

ECO 211.name: Principles of Microeconomics
ECO 211.description: Microeconomics examines markets, firms, allocation and economic policy as domain knowledge.

review.rationale: Microeconomics examines markets, firms, allocation and economic policy as domain knowledge.

ECO 212.name: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECO 212.description: Macroeconomics examines income, employment, banking, growth and economic systems as domain knowledge.

review.rationale: Macroeconomics examines income, employment, banking, growth and economic systems as domain knowledge.

ECO 300.name: Microeconomic Theory and Applications
ECO 300.description: Applies intermediate microeconomic analysis to prices, allocation, individual and firm decisions, and welfare.
ECO 300.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 211 or ECO 213 AND advanced credit in calculus by exam or a minimum C- grade in a calculus course MAS 110 or MTH 130 or MTH 141 or higher.

review.rationale: Applies intermediate microeconomic analysis to prices, allocation, individual and firm decisions, and welfare. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 301.name: Macroeconomic Theory
ECO 301.description: Analyzes the measurement, determination and management of aggregate economic activity.
ECO 301.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 212 AND advanced credit in calculus by exam or minimum C- grade in a calculus course MAS 110 or MTH 130 or MTH 141 or higher.

review.rationale: Analyzes the measurement, determination and management of aggregate economic activity. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 302.name: Microeconomic Theory
ECO 302.description: Analyzes allocation, market competition, factor incomes and public policy using microeconomic theory.
ECO 302.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 211 or ECO 213 AND advanced credit in calculus by exam or a minimum C- grade in a calculus course MTH 141 or higher.

review.rationale: Analyzes allocation, market competition, factor incomes and public policy using microeconomic theory. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 303.name: Macroeconomic Theory
ECO 303.description: Studies aggregate economic activity through intermediate macroeconomic theory.
ECO 303.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 212 or ECO 213 AND advanced credit in calculus by exam or a minimum C- grade in a calculus course MAS 110 or MTH 130 or MTH 141 or higher.

review.rationale: Studies aggregate economic activity through intermediate macroeconomic theory. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 307.name: Public Economics
ECO 307.description: Applies public-finance and microeconomic analysis to government spending, taxation, distribution and policy.
ECO 307.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 213 OR ECO 211 and ECO 212 .

review.rationale: Applies public-finance and microeconomic analysis to government spending, taxation, distribution and policy. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 345.description: Evaluates environmental regulation and economic tradeoffs using externalities, valuation and cost-benefit analysis.

review.rationale: Evaluates environmental regulation and economic tradeoffs using externalities, valuation and cost-benefit analysis. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 351.name: Economics of Development
ECO 351.description: Studies economic development, markets, planning and institutional conditions across countries.
ECO 351.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 213 OR ECO 211 and ECO 212 .

review.rationale: Studies economic development, markets, planning and institutional conditions across countries. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 371.name: Latin America, the Caribbean, and the Global Economy

ECO 371.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 213 OR ECO 211 and ECO 212 .

review.rationale: Examines growth, trade, investment and policy in Latin American and Caribbean economies. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 379.name: The Political Economy of Growth
ECO 379.description: Studies institutional, geographic, cultural and technological determinants of economic growth.
ECO 379.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 213 OR ECO 211 and ECO 212 .

review.rationale: Studies institutional, geographic, cultural and technological determinants of economic growth. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 443.description: Analyzes energy and commodity markets, production, consumption and oil-exporting economies.
ECO 443.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 213 OR ECO 211 and ECO 212 .

review.rationale: Analyzes energy and commodity markets, production, consumption and oil-exporting economies. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

ECO 532.prerequisites: Prerequisite: ECO 213 OR ECO 211 and ECO 212 .

review.rationale: Traces economic doctrines and thinkers historically and their influence on contemporary theory. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

EPS 351.name: Intro to Statistics for the Social, Behavioral, and Educational Sciences
EPS 351.description: Probability, distributions, hypothesis testing and statistical inference are the methods taught.

review.rationale: Probability, distributions, hypothesis testing and statistical inference are the methods taught.

FIN 300.name: Fundamentals of Finance for Non-Finance Majors
FIN 300.description: Introduces financial markets, investments, risk, corporate finance and international finance for nonbusiness students.
FIN 300.prerequisites: Requisite: Non Business Majors. The description states no credit for business students; the explicit requisite is nonbusiness majors.

review.rationale: Introduces financial markets, investments, risk, corporate finance and international finance for nonbusiness students. The classification follows the stated content, not cognate membership or department prefix.

GEG 305.description: Descriptive and inferential statistical methods for spatial data are explicit core content.

review.rationale: Descriptive and inferential statistical methods for spatial data are explicit core content.

GEG 310.description: GIS software is used to answer spatial research questions; the description emphasizes domain use rather than computing infrastructure.

review.rationale: Spatial statistical analysis, especially spatial autocorrelation, is the stated focus.

JMM 331.description: Visual communication encodes information through graphs, maps and diagrams.

review.rationale: Visual communication encodes information through graphs, maps and diagrams.

review.rationale: Probability, inference, hypothesis tests and descriptive statistical methods are central despite the business setting.

MAS 311.name: Applied Probability and Statistics
MAS 311.description: Probability distributions, estimation and hypothesis testing establish a statistical-methods focus.
MAS 311.prerequisites: Prerequisite: MTH 162 or MTH 172 . Or Corequisites: MTH 162 or MTH 172 including equivalents.

review.rationale: Probability distributions, estimation and hypothesis testing establish a statistical-methods focus.

MGT 304.name: Organizational Behavior
MGT 304.description: Organizational behavior centers motivation, leadership, groups, personality and organizational development.

review.rationale: Organizational behavior centers motivation, leadership, groups, personality and organizational development.

MKT 201.name: Foundations of Marketing

review.rationale: Marketing practice covers consumer needs, products, pricing, promotion and distribution.

MKT 301.name: Marketing Foundations

review.rationale: Marketing planning, consumer needs and business case analysis are the subject.

MKT 310.description: Applies behavioral-science findings about consumers to marketing strategy through business cases.
